report.executive_summary: All four pump modules clear the client screen: each has quality at least 80 and five or fewer raw defects. On the single common acceptance-run basis, measured energy ranks P2 first at 12 kWh, then P3 at 52, P1 at 56 and P4 at 58. Under the supplied policy the lowest-energy qualifying package wins, so P2 is the client winner, with a 40 kWh gap over runner-up P3 and 46 kWh over P4. P4 nonetheless stands out as the only zero-defect module, a genuine robustness asset that this report examines separately. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified for every candidate; six open questions are listed for verifier attention.

sections.body: The trusted records give every module a passing profile. P1: quality 84, defects 4. P2: quality 97, defects 1. P3: quality 80, defects 3 — exactly at the quality floor, so any measurement correction could disqualify it. P4: quality 81, defects 0. No candidate sits near the defect ceiling of five, and none fails either gate, so eligibility does not separate the field. Verification effort should therefore go to measurement soundness, especially P3's borderline quality index and P4's spotless defect count, rather than to re-litigating the pass line.
sections.heading: Eligibility Screening

sections.body: Energy is the decision variable, and the spread is large. P2 measures 12 kWh per acceptance run; P3 needs 52, P1 56 and P4 58 on the same fixed flow and head duty. Against the leader the gaps are P3 +40, P1 +44 and P4 +46 kWh, meaning P2 consumes roughly 77–79% less energy than the other three. These are measured facts on one shared test basis, not modelled estimates, so the ranking is stable unless the test protocol itself is questioned. Even runner-up P3 trails by more than four times P2's consumption, a margin the policy resolves unambiguously toward P2 on supplied data.
sections.heading: Energy Ranking and Gaps

sections.body: P4 is the only candidate with zero raw defects, and its quality index of 81 clears the floor with the narrowest margin after P3. That record is the strongest as-built quality signal in the field: fewer defects can mean fewer rework events, tighter process control and lower early-life failure exposure in a transfer loop where a leak or dry-run event is costly. It is also the most expensive profile in energy terms, 58 kWh against P2's 12, a 46 kWh gap per run that compounds over every acceptance cycle. sections.heading: The Zero-Defect Outlier: P4

sections.body: The six open items below are ordered for verifier attention. 1. Scheduled delivery dates and unit cost are unverified for all four packages; P2's 12 kWh reading could still be offset by price premiums unknown to this review. 2. Judging field reliability beyond one acceptance run is impossible on supplied records; wear behavior in a reclamation loop is not covered by the common test basis. 3. Raw inspection logs behind each defect count, especially P4's zero, should be audited before contract award. 4.
